title: Aureus Systems - Activation roadmap & SSO handoff
topics: Initial pilot scope: Dedicated vs Hosted

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Marina Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Aureus CTO), Leo Martinez (Director of ML), Eden Brooks (Head of Security), Samir Vohra (Platform Eng), Maya Ortiz (PM), Oliver Kim (Infra, joined late)

Summary / Topics (auto): Onboarding plan, SSO and RBAC, VPC / private options, Dedicated vs Hosted, pilot scope, runbook and next steps.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Jordan Ellis: Hey everyone, thanks for being on time. This is Jordan from Redwood, I run the AE for this deal; with me is Marina our solutions engineer and Diego who will be your CSM. Quick check — does everyone have the calendar invite?
[00:12] Priya Nair: Yep thanks Jordan. I may need to duck out briefly around 00:38 for an internal call but I should be back.
[00:18] Jordan: Perfect. Quick agenda: security handoff, SSO and RBAC, deployment model choices — like hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC — then action items and pilot timing. Sound OK?
[00:27] Leo Martinez: Sounds good. We're mainly eager to understand the perf tradeoffs and how to keep costs predictable.
[00:32] Marina Chen: Great, I'll start with a high-level on the deployment options and then we'll drill into SSO.
[00:41] Marina: So — at a high level Redwood offers three modes: hosted API for fastest time to value, dedicated reserved capacity if you want predictable throughput and data isolation, and private (VPC or on-prem) for regulated workloads. Each has different network setup and SLA footprints.
[00:55] Eden Brooks: Can you repeat the private option details? We have strict data residency and key mgmt requirements.
[01:02] Marina: Sure — the private option can either be a customer-managed VPC peering with a private control plane, or an on-prem package. We integrate with KMS/HSM for key control, and provide audit logs for all inference requests. For stricter needs we can ship an air-gapped bundle but that is a longer engagement.
[01:18] Priya: Appreciate that. Key thing for us: we need to own the keys and ensure no raw prompts leave the VPC for PII routes. How do you support that?
[01:27] Marina: You can pin routes to run in the private environment only; we also have edge routing policies that respect data tags. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or HSM integrations; our control plane still needs metadata, but we can redact or keep logs in the customer account depending on the deployment model.
[01:43] Samir Vohra: If we do VPC peering, what's the typical network config? Do we need a NAT gateway? What's the egress pattern?
[01:51] Jordan: Good Q. We'll send a network diagram in the packet but in short: for VPC peering you point the traffic to Redwood's inference endpoints over private IP, we typically require specific CIDR allocations and a small set of egress routes for telemetry to the control plane unless you opt for totally private on-prem. NAT is optional depending on your requirements.
[02:09] Marina: Also note, if you pick dedicated capacity we still manage the runtime but it's isolated to your tenant. That reduces cold-start variability and gives firm throughput commitments.
[02:18] Leo: How big is the dedicated minimum? We have some seasonal peaks; want to avoid large commitments.
[02:24] Jordan: There are a few commitment tiers; we can structure a base commitment plus burst credits. We'll get commercial in a separate call, but SE note — Marina will run perf curves so you can make a data driven decision.
[02:35] Marina: On the perf side: our runtime uses continuous batching, prefix caching (KV cache), and quantized kernels where appropriate. For low-latency interactive routes we recommend smaller batch windows and enabled prefix caching for repeated contexts. For higher throughput offline tasks, batching aggressively reduces unit cost.
[02:52] Leo: That caching — does it persist across requests or is it per session?
[02:56] Marina: It's per token prefix cache per model instance, so repeated prompts or system messages across requests can hit the cache and reduce compute. There are cache TTLs you can tune.
[03:06] Eden: Ok, security checklist: we're looking for SOC2, ISO if available, network diagrams, and an audit of where logs are stored. Do you have those docs ready?
[03:15] Jordan: Yes — we have a SOC2 report and a standard security packet. We'll include network diagrams and a privacy note. Diego will coordinate the docs handoff.
[03:23] Diego Patel: I'll compile the packet after the call and share via the secure link. We'll also include our private deployment checklist.
[03:29] Priya: Great. For SSO, we use Okta and have strict group-based RBAC for production access. How do you handle SAML groups and RBAC mapping?
[03:37] Marina: We support SAML and SCIM. Groups can be mapped to roles in Redwood's RBAC. For Private deployments we can also sync group membership via your IdP and enforce role-based route access. We recommend a staging IdP test first to validate the flows.
[03:50] Priya: Perfect. Can we do pre-provisioned roles for engineers vs ML infra vs auditors?
[03:55] Marina: Yep — you can define roles with fine-grained permissions (deploy models, view traces, cost reports, etc.). Auditors can have read-only, token-limited roles.
[04:03] Samir: One more infra question — latency expectations. We're targeting sub-120ms p99 for a 512-token average. Is that achievable?
[04:11] Marina: Depending on model choice and deployment mode, yes — with dedicated capacity and optimized kernels we can approach that for certain smaller models. For larger models or longer context lengths expect higher p99. We'll need to run benchmarks with your prompt set to be certain.
[04:23] Oliver Kim: (joined) Sorry, late. I got the invite. Is there a staging window we need to lock?
[04:28] Jordan: Hey Oliver — yes, we'll propose a 90-minute benchmarking session next week. Marina will follow up with slots.
[04:34] Maya Ortiz: Timeline question — how long from kickoff to pilot? We're aiming for a 6-week runway.
[04:40] Jordan: Typical pilot timelines vary. For a hosted pilot it's faster (1–2 weeks to ingest prompts and validate), for VPC/dedicated it's usually 3–6 weeks because of networking and capacity provisioning. If you prioritize the hosted pilot first we can parallelize the private setup.
[04:55] Priya: We want to avoid any data egress for PII flows — so the private route is important. But we can begin with hosted for less sensitive routes.
[05:04] Marina: That hybrid approach works well. We'll tag routes in config and route them to different environments.
[05:09] Leo: For the pilot success criteria: we'll share a doc with target latency SLO, cost per 1k tokens target, and uptime. Can Redwood surface per-route token-level cost and latency for us?
[05:19] Diego: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, latency histograms and traces. We'll give you a sample dashboard.
[05:26] Priya: And regressions — do you provide alerts if quality drops post-rollout?
[05:31] Marina: We have quality monitors tied to eval sets and prompt groups. We can alert on drift and regression against baseline prompts.
[05:38] Samir: How are rollouts handled? We need canaries and immediate rollback.
[05:42] Marina: Rollouts support canary percentages, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin a percentage to the new model and specify fallback model variants. The runtime will automatically route to fallback on errors or latency spikes.
[05:54] Leo: For the perf test, what telemetry do you need on our side?
[05:58] Marina: We'll run the tests from Redwood's staging agents hitting your staging VPC or hosted endpoint depending on setup. We'll need sample prompts, user distributions, and network egress rules opened for the test window.
[06:10] Priya: I'll have Samir and Oliver coordinate POC infra.
[06:13] Samir: Yep, we'll allocate a staging CIDR and share the contact for peering.
[06:18] Jordan: Ok quick recap of owners — Jordan will send security docs; Marina will prep perf plan; Diego will draft runbook; Priya to share prompts and SLOs; Samir to confirm network window.
[06:28] Priya: Sounds good. Anything else?
[06:31] Maya: Curious about logging retention — we need 7 years for certain audit logs, is that configurable?
[06:37] Diego: We can support longer retention as an add-on; logs can be exported to your object store or kept in the tenant logs depending on the deployment. We'll include retention options in the packet.
[06:48] Eden: One note on redaction — we want to avoid storing raw PII in logs. Is there an automatic redaction path?
[06:55] Marina: We offer request-level redaction rules and can hash or strip designated PII fields before storing traces. For full private deployments you can keep raw logs entirely on-prem.
[07:05] Priya: Great. When should we expect the security packet?
[07:09] Jordan: Diego will send it within two business days, I'll add the network guide and the SAML/SCIM setup doc.
[07:15] Diego: I'll share a secure link to the docs and put the runbook draft in the shared repo.
[07:19] Priya: OK — final ask: can we get a checklist for the pilot kickoff so our PM can track tasks?
[07:25] Jordan: Absolutely — we'll include a pilot checklist (pre-provisioning, IdP test, perf window, eval metrics, rollback plan).
[07:31] Maya: thanks. Any scheduling now for the benchmark session?
[07:34] Marina: I'll follow up with three slots for next week; target one with your infra folks.
[07:39] Oliver: Quick question — do you support pinned quantized model variants so we can trade quality/cost?
[07:45] Marina: Yes — we support model variants and quantization profiles; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization settings per route to meet quality/cost targets. We'll surface recommended profiles post-benchmark.
[07:57] Leo: Great. That's all from me.
[07:59] Priya: Same. I'll review and share the prompt list tonight.
[08:03] Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll send the packet and proposed benchmark slots. Diego will follow with the runbook draft. Meeting adjourned.

End transcript (note: transcription contains occasional mis-hears like "K-V cache" spelled out, names slightly altered).
